title: A review's parked draft is filed with a check, so backlog.py check has no error and the land e2e test stays green
goal: Found in the SP-d3hybrlv review: the orchestrator parked a gap with backlog.py new story and no --check; new only said 'to fill in: checks missing', but backlog.py check counted it an error, and tests.py's land e2e scenario, which clones the working tree, failed on that gate. kb-sprint review step 5 and backlog.md say a parked draft carries a check (or new refuses a story without one outside a planning context), so the review's own checks stay green.

run: import sys;t=open('.claude/skills/kb-sprint/SKILL.md',encoding='utf-8').read();r=t.split('## review SP')[1].split('## close SP')[0];ok='--check' in r;print('parked draft check:',ok);sys.exit(0 if ok else 1)

import sys;t=open('kb/_self/backlog.md',encoding='utf-8').read().split('every other gap is parked')[1].split('\n')[0];ok='--check' in t;print('backlog.md review step: parked draft filed with a check:',ok);sys.exit(0 if ok else 1)

gates.question: How is a review's parked draft kept from failing backlog.py check: a rule in the review step only, or also a refusal in backlog.py new?
options: rule only: review step 5 and backlog.md say a parked draft is filed with --check; new is unchanged
rule and refusal: new also refuses a story filed with no --check outside a planning context
gates.recommendation: rule only: review step 5 and backlog.md say a parked draft is filed with --check; new is unchanged
gates.answer: rule only: review step 5 and backlog.md say a parked draft is filed with --check; new is unchanged
